function: RIS phase-shift configuration by centralized DDPG maximizing the offloading-link rate, then per-vehicle offloading and local-execution power by modified MADDPG, in RIS-aided vehicular edge computing (p. 5-7).
system: BS with M antennas, K = 8 single-antenna vehicles, reflecting RIS with N = 36 elements, 3-bit phases; 1 MHz sub-channels; no carrier frequency stated (p. 3, 5, 9).
method: Reinforcement learning: centralized DDPG for RIS phase shifts, then modified MADDPG (local and twin global critics) for vehicle power allocation; actor 512-256, critic 1024-512-256; 1000 episodes (p. 5-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rician (pure LoS) RIS links, exponential small-scale fading on the direct link, vehicles at 10-15 m/s on an urban road; no external dataset (p. 4, 9).
test_conditions: 1000 training episodes of 100 slots (p. 9); tests of 50 slots per round averaged over 10 rounds (p. 8); arrival rate swept 1-4 Mbps (p. 10).
baselines: Learned: fully centralized DDPG and TD3 applied to the same problem; non-learned: NO-RIS and random RIS phase shift (Figs. 6-7, p. 9-10).
metrics: Reward convergence, power consumption and buffer length (total and per user) versus task arrival rate; percentage reductions versus NO-RIS and centralized DDPG (p. 9-11).
complexity: Big-O training complexity of DDPG, TD3, and modified MADDPG in actor and critic gradient and update costs (GA, GC, UA, UC); no operation counts or runtime (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 4: "is modeled as the Rician fading with the pure LoS component"; own path-loss and fading model (Eqs. 3-7). No 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, QuaDRiGa, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 8: "We conduct tests based on the trained model, where each round contains 50 test slots". Figs. 6-7 (p. 10) sweep the task arrival rate, but the paper does not state that a model trained at 3 Mbps (Table I) is reused, and reports no new scenario, band, or fine-tuning.
q3_support: p. 9: "we compare it with the traditional centralized DDPG and TD3 algorithm" (learned); p. 10: "the schemes without RIS assistance and with random RIS phase-shift" (non-learned).
q4_support: p. 8: "the complexity of the mentioned algorithms will be demonstrated as follows", with Big-O expressions for DDPG, TD3, and modified MADDPG; symbolic training cost, no operation counts or runtime.
q5_support: p. 2: "https://github.com/qiongwu86/DDPG-RIS-MADDPG-POWER" is given in footnote 1, which says the source code has been released.
notes: Area 3: the DDPG-learned RIS phase shifts (p. 5-6) are a physical-layer decision learned jointly with offloading and local power (p. 7), so above_phy does not apply. The BS is said to have M antennas (p. 3), but M is never given a value and the channel gain is scalar (Eq. 8, p. 4). q4 rests on a symbolic Big-O training expression (p. 8); reviewer to confirm. q3 counts DDPG and TD3 as the learned baselines and NO-RIS and random RIS as the non-learned ones (Figs. 6-7, p. 10). PDF title: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Aided Vehicular Edge Computing: Joint Phase-shift Optimization and Multi-User Power Allocation, arXiv preprint 2407.13123v2 (p. 1); the DOI is not printed, so the match rests on the file name.
